headline: Anthropic’s IPO Valuation Soars to $2 Trillion as Revenue Hits $11.5 Billion
deck: The AI company’s aggressive $190-200 billion 2028 revenue forecast underpins investor bets that its IPO could be the most lucrative in tech history.
body: Anthropic’s initial public offering is shaping up to be the most audacious in tech history, with investors placing a $2 trillion valuation on the AI company—despite revenue barely crossing $11.5 billion in the second quarter. Sources familiar with early IPO meetings led by CFO Krishna Rao tell CNBC that no valuation figures have been formally discussed with investors, yet the appetite for a blockbuster deal is undeniable. The disconnect between the company’s current performance and its desired valuation underscores the frenzy around AI stocks and the premium investors are willing to pay for growth potential.

At the heart of the debate is Anthropic’s revenue forecast: $190 to $200 billion by 2028, a figure Reuters reports is central to the company’s IPO strategy. For context, that projection would require the company to nearly double its revenue every year for the next four years—a pace that has drawn skepticism from analysts at Fortune. The gap between the forecast and the company’s current trajectory raises questions about whether the valuation is rooted in reality or hype.

Anthropic’s second-quarter revenue of $11.5 billion, as reported by Bloomberg, is impressive but still a fraction of the scale implied by a $2 trillion valuation. The company’s underlying business, analysts argue, may not yet justify the price tag investors are assigning. Fortune’s analysis suggests that while revenue is growing rapidly, the company’s profitability and market dominance remain unproven at the scale implied by such a lofty valuation.

The stakes are high. A successful IPO at this valuation would give Anthropic the capital to accelerate its AI research, compete with giants like OpenAI and Google, and expand into new markets. But if the company’s growth stalls or fails to meet its own projections, it could face a reckoning similar to other tech darlings that crashed after overvalued debuts. The pressure is on Anthropic to deliver on its promises—or risk becoming another cautionary tale.

Meanwhile, Krishna Rao’s role in these early IPO discussions signals the company’s seriousness about going public, even as Bloomberg’s revenue data suggests the business is still in a high-growth phase. Rao’s silence on valuation details, as reported by CNBC, leaves investors guessing just how aggressive Anthropic plans to be in its public debut. The lack of transparency is fueling both excitement and unease in equal measure.

Gizmodo reports that some investors are already pricing in a valuation of $2 trillion, a figure that would dwarf even the most optimistic tech IPOs in history. Such expectations hinge entirely on Anthropic’s ability to meet its revenue forecast, a gamble that analysts at Fortune warn could backfire if the company’s growth slows or competition intensifies. The disconnect between investor enthusiasm and business fundamentals is widening by the day.

The IPO’s success or failure will hinge on whether Anthropic can convince the market that its revenue forecast is achievable. With $11.5 billion in quarterly revenue, the company has a foundation, but the leap to $190-200 billion by 2028 is monumental. Bloomberg’s data shows that revenue growth has been strong, but the company’s profitability and market position remain untested at the scale required to justify a $2 trillion valuation.

As the IPO process unfolds, the tension between ambition and reality will only grow. Anthropic’s CFO is navigating uncharted territory, with investors betting big on an AI company that has yet to prove it can sustain such explosive growth. The question now is whether the market will reward the hype—or punish it.
